newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem president vows return to key Bosnian town.
newsitem.headline: Moslem president vows return to key Bosnian town.

text.p: Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic vowed on Sunday to regain the strategic Serb-held town of Brcko for thousands of Moslem refugees gathered for an election rally not far away.
"We shall return there, with God's help, very soon. We shall return to other places too, but first to Brcko," he said in a speech at a rally of his SDA party broadcast by state radio and television.

Brcko is a northern town on the Sava River controlled by the Bosnian Serbs who captured it in 1992 and expelled thousands of Moslems and Croats. The town lies along a strategic corridor linking Serb-held areas of Bosnia.
Control of Brcko was left unresolved during the painstaking U.S.-brokered Bosnian peace negotiations in Dayton, Ohio, in November last year.
The town is perhaps the most volatile flashpoint in Bosnia and the two sides remain deeply divided over the issue.
Bosnian Serbs have been stalling the issue by insisting that the arbitration should not involve the town itself, but the area around it.
The Moslem-led government insists on the return of refugees and needs the northern outlet for its commercial ties with Europe.
Izetbegovic told the SDA rally on Bosnian government territory a few km (miles) south of Brcko that he came to the rally to tell the refugees that they would go back to their homes.
The crowd responded with loud cheers and chants of: "Alija, Alija!"

With Bosnia-wide general elections set for September 14 under the terms of the peace accord, the political parties have stepped up their campaigning with nationalist parties playing hard for refugee votes.

The elections are supposed to reunify the war-torn country by creating joint institutions for Moslems, Serbs and Croats, but analysts say they will only confirm the three main nationalist parties' grip on power.
